title: The Discovery Sprint
role: You lead the cryptographic discovery sprint for an enterprise.
objective: Build a trustworthy asset picture within five weeks, inside your authorisation.
environment: The asset register is incomplete. You have authority over the corporate network and your own cloud accounts. Partners and other tenants are not yours.

state_variables.coverage: Coverage of the estate, starts at 10
state_variables.data_quality: Quality of the data, starts at 80

choices.text: Define in-scope ranges with written authorisation from their owners, starting with networks and cloud accounts you own.
choices.feedback: Correct. Active scanning needs authorisation, and a written scope protects you and the owners.

choices.text: Scan every address you can reach, including partners and other tenants.
choices.feedback: More coverage, but unauthorised scanning is an offence in many places and can disrupt other organisations' systems.
People remember what they built, not what exists; interviews alone miss shadow assets.

stages.decision_prompt: How do you collect the data?

choices.text: Combine passive sources (flow logs, DNS, certificate transparency), active scans in agreed windows, and cloud inventory APIs.
choices.feedback: Correct. Independent sources reveal what any one method misses.

choices.text: Run one aggressive full-port scan on production in business hours.
choices.feedback: An unplanned aggressive scan can disrupt production and breaks the agreed change windows.

choices.text: Run one scan once and treat it as complete.
choices.feedback: A single snapshot is a lower bound and ages immediately.

stages.narrative: You have findings and the register.

choices.text: Compare both ways: list shadow assets (found, not registered) and stale records (registered, not found), and assign owners.
choices.feedback: Correct. The differences in both directions are the findings, and each needs an owner.

choices.text: Delete unknown assets from the report to keep it tidy.
choices.feedback: That hides precisely the assets most likely to be unmanaged.

choices.text: Add everything found to the register with no owner.
choices.feedback: An asset with no owner will not be fixed or classified.

stages.decision_prompt: How do you keep the picture current?

choices.text: Schedule recurring discovery, alert on drift against the baseline, and keep the raw evidence.
choices.feedback: Correct. Estates change; a recurring process is what keeps the inventory true.
It starts ageing the day it is delivered.

choices.text: Ask teams to self-report each quarter.
choices.feedback: Self-reporting misses what teams do not know they have.

stages.narrative: The programme board reviews the sprint.

bands.title: Trustworthy picture
bands.text: SUCCESS. The sprint produced a broad, reconciled, owner-assigned picture within authorisation and on time.

bands.title: Useful but incomplete
bands.text: PARTIAL. The picture is useful but narrower, noisier or slower than it could have been.

bands.title: Not trustworthy
bands.text: AT RISK. The scope was breached or the result is too incomplete to rely on.

resolution.concept_reveal: Discovery is authorised, multi-source and repeated. Reconcile findings with the register in both directions, keep unowned items visible, and treat any single scan as a lower bound.

replayability_note: Scoping choices change coverage and compliance differently.
